newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan nuclear plant toilet fire gives brief scare.
newsitem.headline: Japan nuclear plant toilet fire gives brief scare.

text.p: A small fire in a toilet at a Japanese nuclear power plant on Wednesday briefly threw a new scare into the country's beleaguered atomic industry.

A spokesman for Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc said the fire at its Kashiwazaki Kariwa nuclear plant, about 220 km (140 miles) northwest of Tokyo, was immediately extinguished and had no impact on operations at the facility.
"There was absolutely no radiation leakage or impact on plant operations," the TEPCO spokesman told Reuters.
The 1.1 million kilowatt (kw) reactor has been shut since April 24 for routine maintenance checks, and the cause of the fire is under investigation, he said.
The spokesman said the toilet was equipped with an electric heater to process human waste, and the heater could have caused the fire.

TEPCO on Tuesday had to close its 1.1 million kw reactor at its Fukushima No.2 Nuclear Power Plant, about 120 km (75 miles) northwest of Tokyo, after the radioactivity level of exhaust gas briefly went to 20 times higher than normal.
TEPCO has said a pinhole break in the metal cover of a fuel rod in the reactor could have caused the radiation leak which was quickly contained without evacuation of the plant.
